messages:
alexa_support: FYI ACME called in — their integration started seeing a spike of 429s about 09:14 after we pushed the per-key quota tweak. They say error rate ~18% on requests and latency spikes.

mike_engplatform: thanks. which tweak? the per-tenant burst cap we rolled this morning?

alexa_support: yes, the new per-key burst cap (policy id `burst-cap-v3`). Rollout started 08:50, canary 10% -> 25% -> 100% over 2h.

jia_engsre: attaching quick curl repro from ACME test key — they sent steady 120 rps for 2m and got intermittent 429s.

alexa_support: ```bash
# from ACME support repro
for i in {1..240}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-TEST" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate; done
```

jia_engsre: sample responses: 
```
429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 3
{x-request-id: 01F...}
```
Looks like short-lived token-bucket drain, bursts hit new per-key bucket sooner.

tomas_oncall: can we confirm traffic was actually bursty? metrics?

mike_engplatform: checking dashboards — I see ACME client app had a ramp from 20->120 rps at 09:12 for ~3m, then sustained 80 rps. Canary % was at 40% at that time.

sarah_custsuccess: ACME says they didn't change clients; they have a retry loop too so 429s amplified. They're asking for immediate mitigation.

jia_engsre: mitigation options: 1) rollback `burst-cap-v3` to previous thresholds for canary cohorts, 2) temporarily bump per-key limit for ACME via whitelist, 3) tweak gateway smoothing to allow short spikes. Fastest is rollback or whitelist.

mike_engplatform: deploy-bot: we pushed `burst-cap-v3` at 08:50 canary rollout. Status?

deploy-bot: deploy "burst-cap-v3" started 2026-03-17T08:50Z -> canary 40% (08:50-09:10), 100% at 09:30. No errors in deploy pipeline.

tomas_oncall: recommend rollback to previous policy for canary cohorts immediately and open a quick postmortem. Need runbook link?

jia_engsre: agreed. I'll prepare rollback command. Mike, can you approve a whitelist patch for ACME while rollback goes out? that gives them breathing room.

mike_engplatform: approve. go ahead.

jia_engsre: rollback plan snippet: ```json
{
  "policy": "burst-cap-v2",
  "scope": "canary",
  "apply_at": "immediate"
}
```
I will run `rctl policy apply --id burst-cap-v2 --scope canary --force` and monitor error rates.

alexa_support: ACME contact is on the line, I'll notify them of temporary whitelist too.

mike_engplatform: whitelist patch to increase key `sk-acme-ORG` burst limit to 300 rps for 30m: `authctl keys update --key sk-acme-ORG --burst 300 --ttl 30m`

sarah_custsuccess: ACME appreciated the quick mitigation, flagged they'd rather not have to change client behaviour. Please note for postmortem: retry loop amplification and canary timing.

jia_engsre: rollback executed at 09:22. initial metrics: 429 rate down from 18% -> 1.5% within 90s. latency normalized. Monitoring for 15m.

tomas_oncall: filing incident tracker entry and tagging for policy tweak follow-up: root cause hypothesis = aggressive per-key burst cap without accounting for client-side retry/backoff.

mike_engplatform: follow-ups: (1) tighten canary ramp windows and gating based on error spike detection, (2) add safety whitelist flow for top-tier customers, (3) add a short-circuit to pause policy rollout if 5xx/429 > 5% in any region during canary.

alexa_support: ACME confirmed service ok after whitelist + rollback. Closing customer escalation but keeping oncall/eng-platform looped for the postmortem. :thumbsup:

jia_engsre: I'll create a short eval harness to replay ACME traffic pattern against `burst-cap-v3` to tune thresholds before re-proposing.

mike_engplatform: thanks team. I'll own the rollout playbook updates and add the gating rule.

deploy-bot: incident logged: INC-2026-317-09 — policy rollback action recorded.
